how do i turn off fractional shares

Setup → Real money, Schwab, Webull and Claude (for later) → Settings → Fractional shares (Alpaca and the simulation) → Off: whole shares only, then press Save settings. With it on, the bot can buy parts of a share at Alpaca and in the simulation, at least $1 at a time, only for stocks Alpaca allows. Schwab and Webull are whole shares only either way, so pricey stocks are skipped there. A stock whose single share costs more than a position's budget gets a "too pricey" tag on the watchlist.

i have about 5k sitting in my schwab account, will the bot use all of it?

No. It only uses up to the real-money cap you set in Setup (your plan is $50), whatever else is in the account. Its checkbook only holds the money and positions it opened itself, so it never touches your other cash or stocks. Before buying it also checks the cash the broker says is available and spends the smaller amount. Kestrel treats Schwab as a cash account, so it only spends settled money there.

does kestrel short stocks

No. Every method only buys and later sells what it owns; it never bets on a stock falling. TJR's model is coded long only on purpose: shorting it lost in every version of the 16-year test (-0.24R per trade on daily charts), and the bot doesn't short. It also never borrows money.

top of the app says autopilot last seen 45 min ago

The autopilot checks in every 5 minutes, and the pill turns to a warning once it hasn't checked in for 12 minutes or more. Usually the Mac was asleep; the Right now line on the Summary tab asks the same. Wake the Mac, keep it plugged in, and if you close the lid, turn on lid-closed mode in Setup step 2. If Setup shows "on · not running" or a Last problem line, the autopilot itself stopped; it normally restarts on its own. A job that gets stuck makes it restart itself after 30 minutes.

why compare tjr with random trades

Because a stop and a 2-to-1 target can look profitable on their own. The placebo buys at random moments in the same 9:35-11:30am window, with the same trend filter, stop and target, so if TJR's setup can't beat it per trade, the setup itself isn't adding anything. That was a real concern: in the 16-year daily test, TJR longs averaged +0.24R per trade, but random entries with the same stop and target got +0.18R.

alpaca, schwab or webull, which one should i use?

They differ in practical ways, and all three use the same safety rules. Alpaca: paper and real money with the same code, fractional shares, no good faith violations, and it's where the $50 real-money test starts. Schwab: real money only (no paper trading), whole shares only, cash-account rules, and you log in again every 7 days. Webull: a paper (test server) account and real money, whole shares for now, cash-account rules by default, and an approval in the Webull app. Paper can run at Alpaca or Webull, or be simulated on your Mac.

what's danger news

When news is on, the bot reads recent headlines (the last 3 days) from Alpaca's news feed, or Yahoo without keys. If a stock's headlines contain words like offering, bankrupt, chapter 11, trading halt, delist, going concern, SEC charges, fraud, reverse split, default, restatement or subpoena, it won't buy that stock for now. Stocks in play with danger news are skipped too. News never makes it buy anything; it only keeps it away.

what's opening_range_breakout

A day-desk method. The first 30 minutes after the open set the day's opening range, and it has no opinion while that range forms. After that, it buys if the price breaks above the range's high and exits if the price falls back below the middle of the range. Like every day trade, anything still open is sold 10 minutes before the close.

which brokers does kestrel treat as cash accounts?

With the account type on auto: Schwab and Webull are treated as cash accounts, so only settled money is spent. That's the safe assumption; if your account is really margin, these rules only cost a day's wait. Alpaca is treated as margin: every Alpaca account is a margin type, and Alpaca covers unsettled money itself, so there are no good faith violations there. You can set the account type in Setup → Settings. Kestrel never borrows either way.

what happens when i click a stock ticker

A card opens explaining the stock. On top: the company's name, whether it's a stock, ETF or fund, its exchange, sector, industry, size and country, a short description and its website. Under What Kestrel knows: which of its lists it's on and why, whether it's in play today, its next earnings date, its latest score, what each account holds, danger news, and any mistake it won't repeat with it. Then its finished trades in that stock and recent news. It works in the watchlist, positions, trades, activity, the stock list, and on the phone screen.

what has to happen before kestrel can trade my real money?

Four locks all have to be open, and each desk (swing and day) earns it separately. 1) The desk's paper results pass the promotion rules: at least 30 trading days of paper trading, it made money, it beat SPY over the same days, and it never dropped more than 10% from its best day. 2) Your ~/AITrader/.env file says LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true. 3) Prices are real-time, meaning Alpaca or Schwab data, not free Yahoo data. 4) You run the promote step and type REAL MONEY exactly. If any one is missing, no real order goes out.

41.6% a year from the ORB paper sounds amazing, should we expect that?

No. The paper has big caveats: it was tested on the same data it was tuned on, it traded long and short, used 4x borrowed money, assumed no slippage, and used tight stops. Kestrel only buys and never borrows. So the bot tests the idea itself: orb_5min (the paper's rules, long only) is one of the day methods it compares in shadow trades, and the after-market report splits day trades into "in play" and "fixed list" so its own results show whether stocks in play actually help.

what's the kill switch and the daily loss limit?

They're two automatic brakes on each desk. Daily loss limit: if a desk is down 3% on the day, it makes no new buys that day. Kill switch: if a desk falls 15% below its best day, it triggers an emergency stop that sells everything that desk owns and halts it; a live desk then drops back to paper. If you set up Pushover, a real-money kill switch or emergency stop alert repeats every minute until you open it.

how can i see what i made on one specific day

Open the Trades tab and find the Profit & loss calendar. Use ‹ › to get to the month, then hover over the day for a quick summary (finished trades, how many won and lost, and the account value change) or click it. Clicking lists the trades that finished that day: the stock, desk, when and at what price it was bought, what it made or lost, and why it sold. If none finished, it tells you how much the account value moved because of stocks it still holds. The Day by day table below has every day's numbers too.

why is my strategy on half size

Because it's been losing so far. Once a strategy has at least 12 finished trades in that account and its average result is below zero, the bot halves its maximum position size: on the swing desk, 12.5% becomes 6.25% of the desk. It's re-checked after every trade, so once the average turns positive it goes back to normal. If it keeps losing clearly over 30+ trades, it gets paused instead.

what is the new p&l calendar

It's the Profit & loss calendar on the Trades tab. Each weekday of the month shows the money made or lost on trades that finished that day, how many trades and how many won, and a Week column totals each week. A line above it sums the month: the total, up and down days, and the best and worst day. Blue is a gain and red a loss, and a deeper color means a bigger day for that month. Hover a day for details, click it for its trades, and use ‹ › for other months.

why do i have to type REAL MONEY, isn't a button enough?

It's the last lock, and it's meant to be deliberate. Every step up in Kestrel needs numbers and a human yes; there are no shortcuts to live trading. Before it asks, it shows which desk will trade real money and that desk's cap, plus the warning: past results don't guarantee future results, only use money you can afford to lose. Anything other than exactly REAL MONEY means not promoted. Going live stays in the Terminal Setup menu, where you type a confirmation, not in the app window or on your phone.

is there a flag or setting that skips the 30 days? i saw --force somewhere

The --force flag belongs to the plan command and only skips the study month's wait when writing trading plans. It's marked TESTING ONLY, and it doesn't touch paper trading or real money. Promotion to live only happens from paper, and it counts the desk's actual paper trading days against the promotion rules. I'm not going to help work around that. If the goal is to start sooner, Start Stage 1 already skips the study month for the swing desk and paper trades momentum right away.

how do i connect my alpaca account

Use Setup → 1. Connect your Alpaca paper account. Sign up at app.alpaca.markets (paper trading needs no money and no approval), switch to Paper Trading, then open API Keys → Generate. Paste the Key ID and the Secret key into Setup and press Save and test. You should see two green checks: one for prices and one for the Alpaca paper account. Test connection rechecks later. The keys are saved only on your Mac, in ~/AITrader/.env, and a running autopilot restarts to use them.

can we add shorting so it makes money when the market drops?

Not today. Kestrel is long only, and its hard rules say it never borrows. The tests so far aren't encouraging either: shorting with TJR's model lost clearly in every version of the 16-year test. The stocks-in-play paper's results came from long and short trades with 4x borrowed money; Kestrel tests a long-only version itself. In falling markets its protection is different: no new momentum buys while SPY is below its 200-day average, stop-losses on what it owns, and the kill switch.

what happens if i hit the pushover monthly limit

Kestrel keeps count of what it sends each month. Pushover's free sending limit is 10,000 messages a month, and once Kestrel has sent 9,500 it only sends urgent alerts (high and emergency priority), keeping the last 500 for those. Routine alerts like buys, sells and daily results are skipped until the next month. A skipped or failed alert never stops trading, and Telegram alerts aren't affected by this count.

what does the autopilot do every day

It wakes every 5 minutes on weekdays (New York time). 9:25am: check-in, login warnings, earnings dates, and a re-scan if the stock list is stale. 9:35am: stocks in play. During market hours: the day desk decides every 5 minutes and the swing desk checks its stops. 3:30pm: no new day trades. 3:45pm: the swing decision. 3:50pm: the day desk sells out. 4:10pm: the study. 4:15pm: the options watcher and the weekly TJR test. 4:20pm: the all-stocks scan. 4:25pm: the after-market report.

what time does the day desk stop trading

On a normal day the market closes at 4:00pm New York time. The day desk opens no new trades from 3:30pm (30 minutes before the close) and sells everything at 3:50pm (10 minutes before). On early-close days, when the market shuts at 1:00pm, those become 12:30pm and 12:50pm. Stop-losses keep working right up to the sell-off.

how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.
